name: OAuth state / PKCE Weaknesses (Login CSRF, Code Interception)
description: Exploits a missing or unvalidated state parameter (OAuth login CSRF - forcing a victim to log in as the attacker), PKCE downgrade or code_challenge stripping (so an intercepted authorization code can be redeemed without the verifier), and implicit-flow access-token leakage via the Referer header or browser history.
notes:
=== MISSING / UNVALIDATED state (login CSRF) ===
  The state parameter binds the /authorize request to the user's session (CSRF token). If absent or unchecked:
  1. Attacker starts a login, captures their own ?code=... at the callback (does NOT complete it).
  2. Attacker tricks the victim into visiting /callback?code=<attacker_code>.
  3. Victim's RP session is now logged in AS THE ATTACKER - victim's data (cards, uploads) flows to the attacker account.
  Test: remove state entirely, or replay a request with a different user's state - does login still succeed?

=== PKCE DOWNGRADE / code_challenge STRIPPING ===
  PKCE binds the code to a code_verifier. Weaknesses:
  - Server accepts token exchange WITHOUT code_verifier when code_challenge was sent (downgrade).
  - code_challenge_method=plain accepted (verifier == challenge, no SHA-256 protection).
  - Server ignores a mismatched verifier.
  Test: send authorize with code_challenge, then redeem at /token with NO code_verifier, or a wrong one.

=== IMPLICIT-FLOW TOKEN LEAK ===
  response_type=token puts the access_token in the URL fragment. Leaks via:
  - Referer header to third-party resources loaded by the callback page.
  - Browser history / proxy logs if copied to the query string.
  - An open redirect that carries the fragment onward.

=== TOOLING ===
  - Burp Repeater: strip state / verifier, replay the /token POST.
  - Burp 'Request Smuggler' not needed; use Repeater + a CSRF PoC (Burp > Generate CSRF PoC).
  - Observe code_challenge_method and whether /token enforces it.

references.title: RFC 9700 - OAuth 2.0 Security Best Current Practice

recommended.note: Redirect_uri abuse is the usual code-interception primitive this chains with.
CORS flaws can exfil tokens that OAuth clients store client-side.
Attack the id_token/access_token JWT once leaked.

defense.why_it_works: When state is absent or unverified the authorization callback is not bound to the initiating session, enabling login CSRF. When PKCE is advertised but not enforced at /token, an intercepted code can be redeemed without the verifier. Implicit-flow tokens in the URL fragment leak through the browser.
defense.prerequisites: A known authorization endpoint and client_id. For login CSRF, the ability to deliver a crafted callback URL to the victim. For PKCE downgrade, a client that initiates PKCE but a server that does not strictly enforce it.
defense.impact: Login CSRF yields victim data captured into an attacker-controlled account; PKCE downgrade enables full code interception and account takeover; implicit-flow leaks expose bearer access tokens.
defense.detection: [MITRE T1190] /authorize requests with no state parameter, repeated use of the same state across sessions/IPs, and /token exchanges that omit code_verifier despite a prior code_challenge. Access tokens appearing in Referer or query strings in logs.
defense.artifacts: IdP and reverse-proxy logs for /authorize (state, code_challenge, code_challenge_method) and /token (presence/absence of code_verifier), plus Referer headers carrying fragments.
defense.splunk_spl:
index=web (uri_path="/authorize" OR uri_path="/token")
| rex field=uri_query "(?<has_state>state=)"
| rex field=form_data "(?<has_verifier>code_verifier=)"
| where uri_path="/authorize" AND isnull(has_state)
defense.elastic_kql: url.path:"/authorize" and not url.query:*state=* or (url.path:"/token" and not http.request.body.content:*code_verifier*)
defense.sentinel_kql:
W3CIISLog
| where csUriStem in ("/authorize","/token")
| extend hasState = csUriQuery has "state="
| where csUriStem == "/authorize" and hasState == false
| summarize count() by cIP, csUriStem
defense.prevention: Require a cryptographically random, single-use, session-bound state and reject callbacks without it. Enforce PKCE (S256 only; reject plain and reject exchanges missing a valid code_verifier). Use the authorization-code flow, never implicit. Set Referrer-Policy: no-referrer on callback pages.

detections.name: OAuth /authorize missing state parameter
detections.logic:
index=web sourcetype=nginx uri_path="/authorize" method=GET
| where NOT match(uri_query, "(^|&)state=")
| stats count by clientip, useragent, uri_query
detections.false_positives: Non-interactive service clients or health checks hitting /authorize.
detections.tuning: Scope to interactive user-agents and require a prior session cookie; baseline legitimate flows that always include state.
